title: CTO Interview with Sirish Munipalli of Moores Lab AI
gist: Moores Lab AI CTO Sirish Munipalli says chip verification has outgrown its teams and context lost in handoffs causes escaped bugs. His company sells simulation-grounded agents (SpecAgent, VerifAgent, DebugAgent, CoverageAgent), stays model-agnostic and offers verification as a service.

insights.claim: Chip verification has outgrown the teams doing it: it takes more than half of project time, only 14% of projects achieved first-silicon success in the 2024 Wilson Research study, and customers cannot hire verification engineers fast enough.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A persistent talent shortage in verification is the demand case for AI verification tools.
insights.locator: What is the biggest challenge your customer is facing?

insights.claim: Context loss across handoffs (architect intent in the specification, designer assumptions in RTL, reconstruction by the verification engineer) often shows up later as escaped bugs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Tools that preserve a single traceable specification address the root cause rather than a single step of the flow.
insights.locator: Underneath that is a quieter problem: context loss

insights.claim: The Moores Lab AI CTO says that across his career at Intel, Qualcomm and Microsoft, the design was rarely the bottleneck and proving it correct was.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Practitioner view supporting investment in verification automation over design automation.
insights.quote: The design was rarely the bottleneck. Proving it correct was.
insights.locator: What brought you to Moores Lab AI?

insights.claim: Moores Lab AI builds agents that carry out the verification workflow rather than assistants that hand over code snippets: VerifAgent creates a UVM environment from the spec, DebugAgent traces failures to causes, and CoverageAgent closes remaining coverage gaps.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Defines the product scope to compare against EDA incumbents' AI features.
insights.locator: Why is your approach to solving this problem unique?

insights.claim: Moores Lab AI grounds every agent in real simulation as the source of truth, on the view that a model's opinion about design correctness is worthless until a simulator agrees.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Simulator-grounded feedback is the safeguard against LLM hallucination in verification.
insights.quote: A model’s opinion about whether a design is correct is worth nothing until a simulator agrees.
insights.locator: Why is your approach to solving this problem unique?

insights.claim: SpecAgent turns datasheets, design notes and addenda into a single living specification where every statement traces to its source and gaps are flagged, and is being extended to generate C and SystemC models for reference and early software virtual platforms.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A spec-centric knowledge base also opens adjacent uses such as virtual platforms for early software development.

insights.claim: The CTO sees three common alternatives (adding people or outsourcing, general-purpose AI coding assistants, and AI features bolted onto existing EDA tools), arguing each falls short because of budget limits, missing spec and simulator knowledge, or untouched workflow between steps.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Shows how an AI-native startup positions against incumbent EDA vendors; watch whether incumbents extend AI across workflows.
insights.locator: What other approaches are being used to solve this problem?

insights.claim: As AI starts generating RTL, the amount of design to check will grow faster than ever and verification becomes the control point for trust, with teams needing auditable evidence of how, by which agent and against which requirement something was verified.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI-generated design raises demand for verification and audit tooling.
insights.locator: What challenges will your customers face in the near future?

insights.claim: More companies are designing their own silicon for AI workloads, and multi-die and chiplet designs multiply the interfaces needing verification, while the talent pool is not growing at that rate.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Custom silicon proliferation expands the verification market and tightens talent constraints.

insights.claim: Customers want AI benefits without their design IP leaving their walls, so deployment and security will decide which verification tools they can use at all.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: On-premise or private deployment is a gating requirement for AI EDA vendors.

insights.claim: Moores Lab AI argues a company whose value is a model will be overtaken by the next frontier release, so it invests in workflows, verification methodology, simulation integration and feedback loops, and stays model-agnostic.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Durable moats for AI application companies lie in workflow and integration, not the underlying model.
insights.quote: A company whose value is a model will be overtaken by the next release.
insights.locator: How has AI changed your business strategy?

insights.claim: Because customers want outcomes rather than licenses alone, Moores Lab AI embeds its engineers alongside customers and offers verification as a service, while using its own agents internally.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Outcome-based, service-heavy delivery suggests AI EDA startups are blending software with services at this stage.
insights.locator: How has AI changed your business strategy?
